name: open-rsa-oaep
description: One RSA-OAEP sealed key blob, recorded with the private fixture key that opens it. RSA-OAEP is a base sealed-blob carrier beside ECDH P-256: the key is wrapped by OAEP directly, with the binding value ahead of it inside the one plaintext, so the blob is exactly one modulus wide - 256 bytes at 2048 bits, base64url to 342 characters - whatever the plaintext holds. THIS IS AN OPEN VECTOR, NOT A SEAL VECTOR. OAEP draws its padding seed inside the crypto library with nothing to inject, so an RSA render is not reproducible and re-sealing input.contentKeyBase64url would produce a different blob every run. What is pinned is the unseal: expected.blob is the fixture, and a regeneration re-emits it verbatim. REPLAY. Import input.rsa.privateKeyJwk as RSA-OAEP over SHA-256 with no label; decrypt expected.blob with a single decrypt call (no internal structure to parse); the plaintext is expected.bind as UTF-8 followed by the 16-byte key. Rebuild the binding from input.binding (dca-bind-v1|c|renderId|contentName, which is expected.bind), take everything ahead of the last 16 bytes as the recovered binding and compare it WHOLE against that value - a prefix compare would open the premiumtext blob under a premium grant - then the last 16 bytes are the key, equal to input.contentKeyBase64url. WRONG-BINDING REFUSAL. The prefix is the whole relabel defence on this carrier: the same blob rebuilt for another coordinate (contentName bodytext) recovers a plaintext whose prefix is not the rebuilt binding, and the open fails closed. The values are canonical, the fixed 16-byte renderId and an ordinary content name, because a vector is what an implementer copies; the format maxima are proved in the unit tests. Every wire value is base64url with no padding.
